_comment: High-performance switch set for the local Linux checkpoints, restored onto Windows.
Every performance path in this branch is off until its environment variable is set:
src/local/performance-switches.h says 'Every path keeps the original behaviour unless its
environment variable is set', and the switch variables start at 0 (for example
kyty_local_native_xpr_mode {0} in src/local/native_xpr.inc). The contributor's own 40 fps
configuration lived in local, uncommitted checkpoint files that are not in the repository,
so a fresh build runs with everything disabled.
The switch names below are the set tools/local/play-demons-souls.py treats as the startup
switch set, plus the ones run-windows.ps1 turns on by itself. Values are the smallest
in-range setting for each switch: InitializePerformanceSwitches aborts the process for a
value outside a switch's range and prints 'Performance switches: ...' for the ones that
took effect, so the console output shows what was applied.
KYTY_DISPATCH_BATCH is deliberately absent: its range is 1..65536 ('dispatches recorded per
submission'), so 1 is likely the least batched setting rather than the best. Add it with
-Set KYTY_DISPATCH_BATCH=<n> once the right value is known.
KYTY_NATIVE_XPR=2 is the verifying mode (the normal path draws and is compared); use it to
check for rendering differences, then go back to 1.
